title: ~했어야 했다 [haesseoya haetda] (Had to)
shortExplanation: Indicates that something 'had to' be done in the past, often expressing regret or missed opportunities.
longExplanation: '~했어야 했다 [haesseoya haetda]' is used to express that something should have been done or occurred in the past, even if it wasn’t. It often carries a sense of regret or a feeling that an opportunity was missed.

examples.sentence: 어제 그 일을 끝냈어야 했는데, 시간이 부족해서 끝내지 못했어요.
examples.romanization: Eoje geu ileul kkeutnesseoya haetneunde, sigani bujokhaeseo kkeutnaeji motaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I should have finished that work yesterday, but I couldn’t because I didn’t have enough time.

examples.sentence: 학원에 가서 공부했어야 했는데, 게임을 하느라고 갈 수 없었어요.
examples.romanization: Hagwone gaseo gongbuhaesseoya haetneunde, geimeul haneurago gal su eopseosseoyo.
examples.translation: I should have gone to the academy and studied, but I couldn’t because I was playing games.

examples.sentence: 커피 대신 물을 마셨어야 했는데, 카페인이 많아서 잠이 안 왔어요.
examples.romanization: Keopi daesin mureul masyeosseoya haetneunde, kapeini manhaseo jami an wasseoyo.
examples.translation: I should have drunk water instead of coffee, but I couldn’t sleep because there was too much caffeine.

examples.sentence: 전화를 받았어야 했는데, 전화기를 못 봐서 받지 못했어요.
examples.romanization: Jeonhwaleul badesseoya haetneunde, jeonhwagireul mot bwaseo badji motaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I should have answered the phone, but I didn’t because I couldn’t see it.

title: ~혹은 [hogeun] (Or)
shortExplanation: Used to express options or alternatives; 'or'.
longExplanation: '~혹은 [hogeun]' is a conjunction used to present two or more alternatives or choices without prioritizing one over another, similar to 'or' in English.

examples.sentence: 당신은 커피 혹은 차를 원하세요?
examples.romanization: Dangsin-eun keopi hogeun chaleul wonhaseyo?
examples.translation: Would you like coffee or tea?

examples.sentence: 이 문제를 해결하기 위해서는 시간 혹은 노력이 필요하겠어요.
examples.romanization: I munjeleul haegyeolhagi wihaeseoneun sigan hogeun noryeogi pilyohagesseoyo.
examples.translation: Time or effort is needed to solve this problem.

examples.sentence: 그는 강아지 혹은 고양이를 키우고 싶어 했어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun gangaji hogeun goyangireul kiugo sip-eo haesseoyo.
examples.translation: He wanted to raise a puppy or a kitten.

examples.sentence: 여름 휴가를 보내기 위해 바닷가 혹은 산에서 휴가를 보낼 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: Yeoleum hyugaleul bonaegi wihae badasga hogeun san-eseo hyugaleul bonael su iss-eoyo.
examples.translation: You can spend your summer vacation at the beach or in the mountains.

title: 후에야 [hueya] (Only after)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate that something happened or was realized only after a certain event or time.
longExplanation: '후에야 [hueya]' is a compound word formed from '후에' (after) and '야' (only). It emphasizes that an action or realization occurs only after a specified event or period has passed – the precondition for what follows.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 날 떠나고 후에야 난 그녀를 얼마나 사랑하는지 알았어요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga nal tteonago hueya nan geunyeoreul eolmana saranghaneunji alatseoyo.
examples.translation: Only after she left me did I realize how much I loved her.

examples.sentence: 시험을 보고 후에야 이 문제의 정답이 무엇인지 기억이 났어요.
examples.romanization: Siheomeul bogo hueya i munjeui jeongdabi mueosinji gieogi nasseoyo.
examples.translation: Only after taking the test did I remember what the correct answer was.

examples.sentence: 나는 대학을 졸업한 후에야 진짜로 배워야 할 것이 무엇인지 이해했어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun daehageul joreophan hueya jinjjaro baewoya hal geosi mueosinji ihaehaetseoyo.
examples.translation: Only after I graduated from university did I understand what I really needed to learn.

examples.sentence: 일을 시작한 후에야 할 일이 얼마나 많은지 알게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Ileul sijakhan hueya hal ili eolmana manheunji alge doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: Only after starting work did I realize how much there was to do.

title: ~흔히 [heunhi] (Commonly, often)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate that an event or situation happens frequently or is commonly known.
longExplanation: '~흔히 [heunhi]' is an adverb used in Korean to demonstrate that something happens frequently, is a common occurrence, or is typically known. It is very similar to English expressions like 'often', 'commonly', 'usually' or 'typically'. It is used in both objective descriptions of facts and in subjective observations.

examples.sentence: 흔히 사람들은 건강한 음식은 맛이 없다고 생각합니다.
examples.romanization: Heunhi saramdeureun geonganghan eumsigeun masi eopdago saenggakhabnida.
examples.translation: People often think that healthy food is tasteless.

examples.sentence: 한국에서는 혼자 살아가는 사람들을 흔히 '싱글'이라고 부릅니다.
examples.romanization: Hangugeoseoneun honja saraganeun saramdeureul heunhi 'single'irago bureubnida.
examples.translation: In Korea, people living alone are commonly referred to as 'singles'.

examples.sentence: 우리는 흔히 우리나라 음식보다 외국 음식을 더 많이 먹습니다.
examples.romanization: Urineun heunhi urinara eumsikboda oeguk eumsigeul deo manhi meokseumnida.
examples.translation: We often eat more foreign food than our country's food.

examples.sentence: 봄이 오면 흔히 피는 꽃인 벚꽃은 많은 사람들에게 잘 알려져 있습니다.
examples.romanization: Bomi omyeon heunhi pineun kkotin beotkkotseun manheun saramdeurege jal allyeojyeo issseubnida.
examples.translation: Cherry blossoms, one of the flowers that commonly bloom in spring, are well known to many people.

title: ~되다 [doeda] (To become)
shortExplanation: Used to express a change into a different state or condition; 'to become'.
longExplanation: '~되다 [doeda]' is used to indicate that someone or something has changed into a new state or condition. It expresses a transformation or transition from one state to another.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 덥다가 갑자기 춥게 되었어요. 그래서 모두 감기에 걸렸어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga deopdaga gapjagi chupge doeeosseoyo. Geuraeseo modu gamgie geollyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: The weather suddenly became cold after being hot, so everyone caught a cold.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 열심히 공부해서 세계에서 가장 젊은 교수가 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun yeolsimhi gongbuhaseo segyeeseo gajang jeolmeun gyosuga doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: She studied hard to become the youngest professor in the world.

examples.sentence: 나의 친구는 한국어를 배워서 번역가가 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Na-ui chinguneun hangugeoreul baewoseo beonyeokgaga doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: My friend studied Korean and became a translator.

examples.sentence: 자그마했던 새끼 고양이가 큰 고양이가 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Jageumahaessdeon saekki goyangiga keun goyangiga doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: The tiny kitten became a big cat.

title: ~잖다 [janda] (You know, isn't it)
shortExplanation: Used to state information the speaker assumes the listener already knows.
longExplanation: '~잖다 [janda]' is a sentence-ending phrase used to indicate the speaker's assumption that the listener is already aware of the information being shared. It's akin to saying 'you know' or 'isn’t it' in English. This grammar point can be used to confirm facts or imply shared knowledge.

examples.sentence: 너 오늘 학교 가야 하잖아, 왜 아직도 놀고 있어?
examples.romanization: Neo oneul hakgyo gaya hajanha, wae ajikdo nolgo isseo?
examples.translation: You have to go to school today, you know, so why are you still playing?

examples.sentence: 우리 내일 시험이 있잖아. 그래서 오늘 공부하려고.
examples.romanization: Uri naeil siheomi issjanha. Geuraeseo oneul gongbuharyeogo.
examples.translation: We have a test tomorrow, you know. So, I plan to study today.

examples.sentence: 너 그 사람을 알잖아, 그런데 요즘 어떻게 지내?
examples.romanization: Neo geu saram-eul al janha, geureonde yojeum eotteoke jinae?
examples.translation: You know that person, don't you? So, how's he doing these days?

examples.sentence: 지금 시간이 늦었잖아, 우린 이제 공부해야 해.
examples.romanization: Jigeum sigani neu-eossjanha, urin ije gongbuhayeya hae.
examples.translation: It's late now, you know, so we should study.

title: ~져/지다 [jyeo/jida] (Become)
shortExplanation: Used to depict changes in state, emotion, condition, or situation, similar to 'become' or 'get' in English.
longExplanation: '~져/지다 [jyeo/jida]' is a conjugation that indicates transformation or change. It can mean 'become' or 'get' and is used to describe shifts in state, feelings, or conditions.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 너무 더워져서 밖에 나가기가 힘들어졌어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga neomu deowojyeoseo bakke nagagiga himdeureojyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: The weather has become so hot that it's hard to go outside.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 학교에서 인기가 많아져서 많은 사람들이 그녀를 알게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun hakgyoeseo ingiga manhajyeoseo manheun saramdeuli geunyeoreul alge doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: She has become popular in school, so many people got to know her.

examples.sentence: 그는 그림을 많이 그리니까, 그림 그리는 실력이 정말 좋아졌어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun geurimeul manhi geurinikka, geurim geurineun sillyeogi jeongmal joahjyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: He has become really good at drawing because he draws a lot.

examples.sentence: 일하는데 집중하니까 시간이 너무 빨리 가버렸어요.
examples.romanization: Ilhaneunde jipjunghanikka, sigani neomu ppalli gabeollyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: Time has gone by so fast because I was focused on work.

title: ~졌다가 [jyeotdaga] (Was once, but)
shortExplanation: Used to express that something was once in a certain state or condition, but then changed again.
longExplanation: '~졌다가 [jyeotdaga]' is used to indicate a sequence where the subject was once in one state and then changed to another—often reverting or fluctuating. It is typically attached to verbs in the past tense.

examples.sentence: 나는 문을 열졌다가 다시 닫았어요. 그런데 친구가 오길 기다릴 수 없어서요.
examples.romanization: Naneun muneul yeoljyeotdaga dasi dadasseoyo. Geureonde chinguga ogil gidaril su eopseoseoyo.
examples.translation: I opened the door, but then closed it again. However, I couldn't wait for my friend to come.

examples.sentence: 그 레스토랑은 며칠 전에 문을 연졌다가 오늘 바로 닫았어요.
examples.romanization: Geu reseutorangeun myeochil jeone muneul yeonjyeotdaga oneul baro dadasseoyo.
examples.translation: That restaurant had opened just a few days ago, but it closed again today.

examples.sentence: 아이들은 컴퓨터 게임을 하다가 숙제를 그만두어야 했어요.
examples.romanization: Aideuleun keompyuteo geimeul hadaga sukjereul geumandueoya haesseoyo.
examples.translation: The kids had to stop playing computer games and do their homework.

examples.sentence: 나의 친구는 직장을 받았다가 한 달 후에 해고되었습니다.
examples.romanization: Naui chinguneun jikjangeul badatdaga han dal hue haegodoeeotseumnida.
examples.translation: My friend got a job, but then got fired after a month.

title: ~즉 [jeuk] (That is to say, namely)
shortExplanation: Used to restate or clarify a point with more detail; 'namely', 'that is to say'.
longExplanation: '~즉 [jeuk]' is a conjunction used in Korean to re-explain or add further details to a statement. It is equivalent to 'namely' or 'that is to say' in English and helps clarify or specify information.

examples.sentence: 이 연구의 결과를 바탕으로 즉, 우리가 본 바로는 지구 온난화는 인간의 활동 때문임이 분명하다.
examples.romanization: I yeonguui gyeolgwareul batangeuro jeuk, uriga bon baroneun jigu onnanhwaneun inganui hwaldong ttaemunimi bunmyeonghada.
examples.translation: Based on the results of this research, that is to say, from what we have seen, it is clear that global warming is due to human activities.

examples.sentence: 그는 국제관계 전문가이다. 즉, 그는 세계의 다양한 나라들 간의 문제를 연구한다.
examples.romanization: Geuneun gukje gwangye jeonmungaida. Jeuk, geuneun segyeui dayanghan naradeul gan-ui munjeleul yeonguhanda.
examples.translation: He is an expert in international relations. That is to say, he studies issues between various countries around the world.

examples.sentence: 이 메일은 너에게만 보낼 것이다. 즉, 너는 이 메시지의 유일한 수신자다.
examples.romanization: I meireun neoegeman bonael geosida. Jeuk, neoneun i mesijui yuilhan susinjada.
examples.translation: I will send this email to you only. Namely, you are the only recipient of this message.

examples.sentence: 그는 내 좋은 친구이다. 즉, 나는 그를 아주 잘 알고 있다.
examples.romanization: Geuneun nae joheun chinguida. Jeuk, naneun geureul aju jal algo itda.
examples.translation: He is a good friend of mine. That is to say, I know him very well.

title: ~지 않을까 싶다 [ji anheulkka sipda] (I think perhaps)
shortExplanation: Expresses an assumption or supposition that something might be; it suggests that the speaker thinks something is likely.
longExplanation: The structure '~지 않을까 싶다' is used to express a guess or speculation about a situation. It conveys uncertainty as well as a hopeful anticipation about what might happen or be true.

examples.sentence: 그가 이번 시험에 잘 볼 수 있을지 않을까 싶어요, 왜냐하면 그는 항상 열심히 공부하고 있거든요.
examples.romanization: Geuga ibeon siheome jal bol su isseulji anheulkka sipeoyo, waenyahamyeon geuneun hangsang yeolsimhi gongbuhago issgeodeunyo.
examples.translation: I think perhaps he might do well on this test, because he is always studying hard.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 나빠지지 않을까 싶어요, 구름이 많아지고 있어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga nappajiji anheulkka sipeoyo, gureumi manhajigo isseoyo.
examples.translation: I think the weather might get worse; the clouds are increasing.

examples.sentence: 오늘 밤에 집에 도착할 수 있을지 않을까 싶어요, 비행기가 시간에 맞춰 출발했어요.
examples.romanization: Oneul bame jibe dochakhal su isseulji anheulkka sipeoyo, bihaengiga sigane matchwo chulbalhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I think perhaps I could reach home tonight since the airplane has departed on time.

examples.sentence: 이번 주말에 영화 보러 갈 수 있을지 않을까 싶은데, 어떻게 생각하세요?
examples.romanization: Ibeon jumal-e yeonghwa boreo gal su isseulji anheulkka sipeunde, eotteohge saenggakhaseyo?
examples.translation: I think perhaps we might go see a movie this weekend; what do you think?

title: ~지 않을까 하다 [ji anheulkka hada] (I guess, I suspect)
shortExplanation: Used to express one's conjecture or prediction; 'I think', 'I guess', 'I suspect'.
longExplanation: '~지 않을까 하다' is used to express a guess or suspicion about a situation when the speaker is not completely sure. It conveys the speaker's uncertainty and expectation about what might be true.

examples.sentence: 내일 비가 올지 않을까 해서 우산을 가져왔어요.
examples.romanization: Naeil biga olji anheulkka haeseo usaneul gajyeowasseoyo.
examples.translation: I brought an umbrella because I thought it might rain tomorrow.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 좋아하는 사람을 만나지 않을까 해서 신경 쓰고 있어요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga joahaneun sarameul mannaji anheulkka haeseo singyeong sseugo isseoyo.
examples.translation: I'm nervous because I suspect she might meet the person she likes.

examples.sentence: 지금 새벽이니까 아마 모든 사람들이 잠들지 않을까 해요.
examples.romanization: Jigeum saebyeoginikka ama modeun saramdeuri jamdeulji anheulkka haeyo.
examples.translation: Since it's dawn now, I guess everyone might be asleep.

examples.sentence: 내 친구가 이번 시험에 합격하지 않을까 해서 축하 메시지를 준비하고 있어요.
examples.romanization: Nae chinguga ibeon siheome hapgyeokhaji anheulkka haeseo chukha mesijireul junbihago isseoyo.
examples.translation: I'm preparing a congratulatory message because I think my friend might pass this exam.

title: ~지 않을래 [ji anheullae] (I don't want to)
shortExplanation: Expresses the speaker's intention not to do something.
longExplanation: '~지 않을래' is a verb ending used in Korean to indicate that the speaker does not want to perform a certain action. It shows a strong personal decision and is typically used in informal contexts.

examples.sentence: 저는 오늘 운동하러 가지 않을래요, 몸이 좀 피곤해서 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun oneul undonghareo gaji anheullaeyo, momi jom pigonhaeseo swigo sip-eoyo.
examples.translation: I don't want to go exercise today because I feel a bit tired and want to rest.

examples.sentence: 저는 너무 많이 먹었기 때문에 디저트는 먹지 않을래요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun neomu mani meogeoss-gi ttaemune dijeoteuneun meokji anheullaeyo.
examples.translation: I don't want to eat dessert because I ate too much.

examples.sentence: 너무 걱정하지 말고, 그 사람은 제가 대신 말하지 않을래요.
examples.romanization: Neomu geogjeonghaji malgo, geu saram-eun jega doae daesin malhaji anheullaeyo.
examples.translation: Don't worry too much; I don't want to speak on your behalf to that person.

examples.sentence: 이 옷이 마음에 들지 않아서 사지 않을래요.
examples.romanization: I os-i ma-eum-e deulji anhasseo saji anheullaeyo.
examples.translation: I don't like this outfit, so I don't want to buy it.

title: ~지요 [jyo] (~지, right?)
shortExplanation: A casual way to seek agreement or confirmation from the listener, similar to 'right?' or 'isn't it?' in English.
longExplanation: ~지요 [jyo] is a commonly used ending in conversational Korean that seeks agreement or confirmation. It softens statements and is often used in friendly dialogues. In English, it can be roughly translated as 'right?' or 'isn't it?'.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 매우 좋지요?
examples.romanization: Nalssiga maeu johjiyo?
examples.translation: The weather is very nice, isn't it?

examples.sentence: 우리는 내일 학교에 가야 하지요?
examples.romanization: Urineun naeil hakgyoe gaya hajiyo?
examples.translation: We have to go to school tomorrow, right?

examples.sentence: 이 영화가 재미있었지요?
examples.romanization: I yeonghwaga jaemiisseotjiyo?
examples.translation: This movie was interesting, wasn't it?

examples.sentence: 그녀는 아직도 학생인 것 같지요?
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun ajikdo haksaengin geot gatjiyo?
examples.translation: She's still a student, right?

title: ~진행하다 [jinhaenghada] (To proceed)
shortExplanation: Used to express the progression or continuation of an action or event.
longExplanation: '~진행하다 [jinhaenghada]' indicates that an action or event is being carried out or continued. It is equivalent to 'to proceed with' or 'to continue' in English and can be used in contexts such as work, study, or any ongoing process.

examples.sentence: 연구팀은 이 이슈에 대해 조사를 진행하고 있습니다. 그들은 다양한 데이터를 수집하면서 정보를 분석하고 있어요.
examples.romanization: Yeongutimeun i isue daehae josareul jinhaenghago itsseumnida. Geudeureun dayanghan dateoreul sujibhamyeo jeongboreul bunseokhago itsseoyo.
examples.translation: The research team is conducting an investigation on this issue; they are analyzing information as they collect various data.

examples.sentence: 오늘 회의를 얼마나 빨리 진행하느냐에 따라서 제 시간에 퇴근할 수 있을지 결정됩니다.
examples.romanization: Oneul hoeuireul eolmana ppalli jinhaenghaneunyae ddalaseo je sigane tuikeunhal su iss-eulji gyeoljeongdoebnida.
examples.translation: Whether I can leave work on time today is decided by how quickly the meeting proceeds.

examples.sentence: 학생들은 공부를 계속 진행하다 보니 시간이 어떻게 지나갔는지도 모르겠습니다.
examples.romanization: Haksaengdeureun gongbureul gyesok jinhaenghada boni sigani eotteoke jinagatneunjido moreugesseumnida.
examples.translation: The students were so engrossed in their studies that they didn’t realize how fast time passed.

examples.sentence: 프로젝트 계획 중, 우리 팀은 문제 해결을 위한 논의를 진행하고 있습니다.
examples.romanization: Peurojekteu gyehoeg jung, uri timeun munje haegyeoreul wihan noniureul jinhaenghago itsseumnida.
examples.translation: During the project planning, our team is proceeding with discussions to resolve the issue.

title: ~차라리 [charari] (Rather, instead)
shortExplanation: Used to express a preference for one option over another; 'rather', 'instead'.
longExplanation: '~차라리 [charari]' is used to indicate that one option is preferable to another, often implying that the chosen option is the lesser of two evils or simply more favorable. It is typically used in the pattern: '[A] 보다는 차라리 [B]'.

examples.sentence: 나는 그냥 집에서 혼자 있기보다는 차라리 밖에서 친구들과 놀러 나갔어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun geunyang jibeseo honja itgibodaneun charari bakeseo chingudeulgwa nolreo nagasseoyo.
examples.translation: I would rather go out and play with friends than just stay home alone.

examples.sentence: 당신이 직접 거짓말하기보다는 차라리 솔직하게 말하면 좋겠어요.
examples.romanization: Dangsini jigjeob geojitmalhagi bodaneun charari soljikhage malhamyeon johgesseoyo.
examples.translation: I'd rather you speak honestly than tell a lie yourself.

examples.sentence: 그 물건을 사지 않기보다는 차라리 돈을 저금하는 것이 낫습니다.
examples.romanization: Geu mulgeoneul saji anhgibodaneun charari doneul jeogeumhaneun geosi natseupnida.
examples.translation: It’s better to save money than to buy that item.

examples.sentence: 그럴 거면 차라리 아무 말도 하지 않는 것이 나아요.
examples.romanization: Geureol geomyeon charari amu maldo haji anneun geosi naayeo.
examples.translation: If that’s the case, I’d rather you said nothing at all.
